ancestors.title: Equations with variables on both sides

description: Learn how to solve the equation 2x + 3 = 5x - 2 with the variable on both sides. We start by visualizing the equation, then isolate the variable by performing the same operations on both sides. Finally, we solve the equation to find the value of the variable.
title: Intro to equations with variables on both sides

ancestors.title: Equations with variables on both sides

description: Solving equations like 20 - 7x = 6x - 6 with the variable on both sides involves a few steps! First, we add or subtract terms from both sides to separate constants and variables to different sides of the equation. Then, we simplify to isolate the variable. Finally, we check our answer by plugging it back into the original equation.
title: Equations with variables on both sides: 20-7x=6x-6

ancestors.title: Equations with variables on both sides

description: To solve the equation (3/4)x + 2 = (3/8)x - 4, we first eliminate fractions by multiplying both sides by the least common multiple of the denominators. Then, we add or subtract terms from both sides of the equation to group the x-terms on one side and the constants on the other. Finally, we solve and check as normal.
title: Equation with variables on both sides: fractions

ancestors.title: Equations with variables on both sides

description: The variable x is in the denominator in 7 - 10/x = 2 + 15/x. We can multiply both sides of the equation by x to turn it into a more familiar, linear form without fractions. From there, we isolate the variable to solve. P.S. x cannot equal zero, because then the equation would be undefined.
title: Equation with the variable in the denominator
